exposure: delivery mode history (caesarean section, spontaneous vaginal deliveries, combination)
Delivery mode history (caesarean section only, spontaneous vaginal delivery only, or a combination)
cohort: Women who gave birth in maternity units in Aberdeen, Birmingham, and Dunedin and responded to questionnaires at 3 months and 12 years postpartum
finding: This study demonstrated that UI persists to 12 years in about three-quarters of women, and that risk was only reduced with caesarean section if women had no other delivery mode.
mod_finding: Women who delivered exclusively by caesarean section were less likely to have persistent UI compared to those who had only spontaneous vaginal deliveries, while women who had a combination of caesarean section and spontaneous vaginal births did not have a reduced risk of persistent UI.
country: United Kingdom (Aberdeen, Birmingham) and New Zealand (Dunedin)
